podcasts.title: The Missing Layer for Personal AI | First Person Labs’ Ken Liu
podcasts.description:
AI agents are getting smarter, but every new agent still has to learn who you are. What if your preferences, priorities, relationships, and digital context could move with you instead?

First Person Labs co-founder Ken Liu joins a16z’s Martin Casado and Joel de la Garza to introduce Second, a personal context layer designed to understand what you’re doing across your digital life and make that context available to the agents you choose.

They discuss how Second can proactively connect information across conversations and applications, why protecting such personal data requires a different security architecture, and the longer-term vision of AI that doesn’t just respond to prompts, but understands enough context to know when and how to help.

podcasts.title: Can AI Learn to Improve Itself? | Recursive Self-Improvement
podcasts.description:
For decades, the idea of AI improving itself was just a thought experiment. Today, AI is already helping researchers at frontier labs run experiments, write code and test ideas faster. Mark Chen says OpenAI has built “AI research interns.” So how far are we from AI that can do the research on its own?

In our first episode of Working Theory, a16z general partner Sarah Wang explores recursive self-improvement with two leading AI researchers: Mark Chen, Chief Research Officer at OpenAI, and John Schulman, co-founder and Chief Scientist of Thinking Machines Lab, and co-founder of OpenAI.

They cover what RSI actually means, why research taste is so hard to teach, and why AI may be one of our best tools for solving alignment.

podcasts.title: Brad Gerstner & Geoffrey Canada - Raising the Floor for Every American Child - [Invest Like the Best, EP.501]
podcasts.description:
My guests today are Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital, and Geoffrey Canada, founder of Harlem Children's Zone. Geoffrey spent decades helping disadvantaged kids get a great education, but it takes more than that to achieve the American dream. Without savings, you’re one emergency away from bankruptcy.

Brad set out to change that. When he first called me about Invest America in 2020, I thought it was a fool’s errand. Six years later, nearly 70 million children have accounts in their name, and every American newborn receives $1,000 in the S&P 500. The challenge now is getting families to claim their accounts, since free money is surprisingly hard to give away.

Brad and Geoffrey believe even a small nest egg, when given a head start on compounding, can help rebuild faith in capitalism. As AI reshapes the economy, they see these accounts as the basis of a new social contract built on ownership and participation, where every child owns a piece of the upside.

Please enjoy my conversation with Brad and Geoffrey.

podcasts.title: USA v/s China AI Labs. OpenSource AI after Jensen leaves NVIDIA
podcasts.description:
More than 1.5 GW of chips are in China that shouldn’t be. Unwinding that web could reshape open-source AI.

“In our view, there’s more than one and a half gigawatts of chips in China that are not supposed to be there according to US law. How they get there, that whole web, that’s what’s going to unwind.”

“If NVIDIA can no longer support the open-source ecosystem, because that was Jensen’s primary goal, does that mean the open-source ecosystem falls away?”

“Now open source looks a lot weaker with NVIDIA down and out. Anthropic looks much more likely to get a complete monopoly or a duopoly. This bodes really well for Anthropic’s IPO next week.”

“They’re more diverse in what chips they use than any other company in the world.”

podcasts.title: Alex Imas & Tyler Cowen | AI Is Moving Fast. Why Isn’t the Economy?
podcasts.description:
AI capabilities are improving fast. But will the economy move just as quickly? a16z General Partner Erik Torenberg sits down with Google DeepMind economist Alex Imas and economist Tyler Cowen to examine how advances in AI translate into growth, jobs, wages, and productivity.

They debate what it would take to reach double-digit economic growth, why bottlenecks and falling AI costs could slow the impact, and whether frontier lab valuations require much larger productivity gains.

They also explore the “economics of intelligence,” including why the bigger shift may come not from smarter individual agents, but from AI agents learning to coordinate at scale.

podcasts.title: [REPLAY] Paul Enright – Inside Long-Short Equity Investing (Capital Allocators, EP.266)
podcasts.description:
Paul Enright is a private investor managing his own capital under single family office, Krainos Capital. Paul opened Krainos after a dozen years at Viking Global Investors, the multi-billion dollar long-short equity hedge fund that also has been one of the most successful breeding grounds for talent in the industry. He has a deep understanding of intricacies of long-short equity investing and a knack for explaining it well.


Our conversation covers Paul's career path to Viking, training while there, and advice to early-career investors. We dive into the distinction between business analysis and stock picking, and the importance of portfolio management to investment success. In the process, we discuss liquidity, shorting, portfolio rebalancing, incentive compensation, and market structure. We close with Paul's approach to managing his own money and his answers to a terrific set of questions sourced from his Twitter feed before the show.
